verses.text: The Philistines gathered their armies for war. They came together at Sokoh in Judah and camped between Sokoh and Azekah, at Ephes Dammim.
Saul and the Israelites gathered and camped in the Valley of Elah, and they lined up for battle to face the Philistines.
The Philistines stood on one hill and the Israelites on another, with the valley between them.
A champion named Goliath, from Gath, came out of the Philistine camp. He was about three metres tall.
He wore a bronze helmet and a coat of armour made of bronze scales, weighing about fifty-seven kilograms.
He had bronze armour on his legs, and a bronze spear was slung on his back.
The handle of his spear was as thick as a weaver's rod, and its iron point weighed about seven kilograms. The man carrying his shield walked ahead of him.
Goliath stood and shouted to the soldiers of Israel, "Why are you lining up for battle? I am a Philistine, and you are Saul's servants. Choose one of your men and have him come down to me.
If he can fight and kill me, we will become your slaves. But if I beat him and kill him, you will become our slaves and serve us."
Then the Philistine said, "Today I challenge the armies of Israel! Give me a man so we can fight each other."
When Saul and all the Israelites heard what the Philistine said, they were terrified and lost their courage.
Now David was the son of Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons, and in Saul's time he was very old.
Jesse's three oldest sons had followed Saul to the war. The oldest was Eliab, the second was Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.
David was the youngest. The three oldest followed Saul,
but David went back and forth from Saul to look after his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening and stood there.
One day Jesse said to his son David, "Take this basket of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread, and hurry to your brothers in the camp.
Take these ten cheeses to the commander of their unit. See how your brothers are, and bring back some news from them.
They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines."

Early in the morning David left the sheep with someone to look after them, loaded up and set out, as Jesse had told him. He reached the camp just as the army was going out to its battle positions, shouting the war cry.
Israel and the Philistines were lining up facing each other.
David left his things with the man in charge of supplies, ran to the battle line and asked his brothers how they were.
As he was talking with them, Goliath, the Philistine champion from Gath, stepped out from his lines and shouted his usual challenge, and David heard it.
Whenever the Israelites saw the man, they all ran from him in great fear.

The Israelites had been saying, "Do you see this man who keeps coming out? He comes out to challenge Israel. The king will give great riches to the man who kills him. He will also give him his daughter in marriage, and his family will not have to pay taxes in Israel."

David asked the men standing near him, "What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and takes away this shame from Israel? Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should challenge the armies of the living God?"
They told him what would be done for the man who killed him.

When Eliab, David's oldest brother, heard him speaking with the men, he became angry with him and asked, "Why have you come down here? And who did you leave those few sheep with in the desert? I know how proud you are and how wicked your heart is. You only came down to watch the battle."
"Now what have I done?" said David. "Can I not even speak?"
He then turned away to someone else and asked the same question, and the men answered him as before.
What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him.
David said to Saul, "Let no one lose heart because of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him."
Saul replied, "You are not able to go out against this Philistine and fight him. You are only a young man, and he has been a warrior since he was young."
But David said to Saul, "Your servant has been looking after his father's sheep. When a lion or a bear came and carried off a sheep from the flock,
I went after it, struck it and rescued the sheep from its mouth. When it turned on me, I grabbed it by its hair, struck it and killed it.
Your servant has killed both the lion and the bear. This uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has challenged the armies of the living God.
The LORD who rescued me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Saul said to David, "Go, and the LORD be with you."
Then Saul dressed David in his own clothes. He put a coat of armour on him and a bronze helmet on his head.
David put on Saul's sword over the clothes and tried walking around, because he was not used to them. "I cannot go in these," he said to Saul, "because I am not used to them." So he took them off.
Then he took his shepherd's stick in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the stream, and put them in the pocket of his shepherd's bag. With his sling in his hand, he went toward the Philistine.
Meanwhile, the Philistine, with his shield carrier in front of him, kept coming closer to David.
He looked David over and saw that he was only a young man, healthy and handsome, and he looked down on him.
He said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come at me with sticks?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
"Come here," he said, "and I will give your flesh to the birds and the wild animals!"

David said to the Philistine, "You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Heaven's Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have challenged.

This day the LORD will give you into my hands. I will strike you down and cut off your head. This very day I will give the dead bodies of the Philistine army to the birds and the wild animals, and the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel.
All those gathered here will know that the LORD does not save by sword or spear. The battle belongs to the LORD, and he will give all of you into our hands."
As the Philistine moved closer to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.
Reaching into his bag, he took out a stone, slung it and struck the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell face down on the ground.
So David won the fight against the Philistine with a sling and a stone. Without a sword in his hand, he struck down the Philistine and killed him.

David ran and stood over him. He took hold of the Philistine's sword and pulled it out of its holder. After he killed him, he cut off his head with the sword. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.

Then the men of Israel and Judah rose up with a shout and chased the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.
When the Israelites came back from chasing the Philistines, they robbed their camp.
David took the Philistine's head and brought it to Jerusalem. He put the Philistine's weapons in his own tent.

As Saul watched David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is that young man?" Abner replied, "As surely as you live, Your Majesty, I do not know."
The king said, "Find out whose son this young man is."
As soon as David came back from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul. David was still holding the Philistine's head.
"Whose son are you, young man?" Saul asked him. David said, "I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem."
